questions.stem: A stage theory of development explicitly emphasizes which of the following principles"
questions.explanation: A stage theory of development explicitly emphasizes the principle of discontinuity of development. It suggests that individuals progress through distinct, qualitatively different stages, marked by specific behaviors or characteristics. This perspective contrasts with the notion of continuous, gradual change and highlights the idea that development occurs in discontinuous, stage-like transitions.
questions.supporting_excerpt: A stage theory of development explicitly emphasizes which of the following principles" — Answer: (B) Discontinuity of development

questions.stem: Cognitive engagement of children within a constructive classroom can be facilitated by– (i) Children’s talk (ii) Emotions of a teacher (iii) Positive interpersonal relationships among children (iv) Externally imposed discipline

Externally imposed discipline, which is not part of this combination, does not align with the constructivist emphasis on intrinsic motivation and self-regulation.

questions.stem: While_______agencies of socialisation are predominantly important in infancy, agencies of socialization also____become important in early childhood.
questions.explanation: Primary agencies of socialization, like family and caregivers, are predominantly important in infancy as they lay the foundation for a child's social and emotional development. It is where children first learn about their culture, language, values, and basic social norms. Family members serve as role models and provide emotional support. Secondary agencies of socialization, such as schools and peer groups, become increasingly important in early childhood as they introduce children to a wider social world and provide additional learning experiences. Schools teach academic knowledge and skills and also socialize students into the norms of their society.
questions.supporting_excerpt: While_______agencies of socialisation are predominantly important in infancy, agencies of socialization also____become important in early childhood. — Answer: (B) primary; secondary

questions.stem: Physical growth and development follow the and principles of development.

options.text: integration (simple to complex); differentiation (complex to simple)
c e p h a l o c a u d a l ( t o p - d o w n ) ; proximodistal (inner to outer)
p r o x i m o d i s t a l ( t o p - d o w n ) ; cephalocaudal (inner to outer)
differentiation (simple to complex); integration (complex to simple)

questions.expected_answer: c e p h a l o c a u d a l ( t o p - d o w n ) ; proximodistal (inner to outer)
questions.explanation: Cephalocaudal: This principle states that development tends to progress from the head (cephalic) to the feet (caudal). In other words, during early development, the head and upper body develop before the lower body and legs. Proximodistal: This principle suggests that development begins at the center of the body (proximal) and extends outward (distal). So, a child's core muscles and abilities develop before those in the extremities.
questions.supporting_excerpt: Physical growth and development follow the and principles of development. — Answer: (B) c e p h a l o c a u d a l ( t o p - d o w n ) ; proximodistal (inner to outer)

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an internal attribution for failure"

options.text: I received a low grade because the teacher is a tough grader.

I didn't get good marks because the teacher was biased.
I failed the test because my friends were distracting me.

questions.expected_answer: I failed the test because I didn't study enough.
questions.explanation: Internal attribution for failure refers to the belief or explanation that a person assigns to their own shortcomings, mistakes, or failures based on factors that are within their control, such as their personal abilities, effort, decisions, or actions. 'I failed the test because I didn't study enough' is an example of an internal attribution for failure. This statement attributes the failure to an internal, personal factor - not studying enough. It suggests that the cause of the failure is within the individual's control and related to their own actions or choices. Internal attributions for failure typically involve factors such as effort, ability, or decisionmaking by the individual.
questions.supporting_excerpt: Which of the following is an example of an internal attribution for failure" — Answer: (B) I failed the test because I didn't study enough.

questions.stem: The primary goal of learning should be:
questions.explanation: The primary goal of learning is typically to equip individuals with the ability to think critically and apply their knowledge in practical and meaningful ways. Critical thinking is a foundational skill that allows individuals to analyze, evaluate, and apply knowledge effectively. It goes beyond memorization and rote learning by encouraging students to think critically, solve problems, and make informed decisions. The development of critical thinking skills enables learners to not only understand facts but also apply them in various contexts, adapt to new challenges, and engage in meaningful and lifelong learning.
questions.supporting_excerpt: The primary goal of learning should be: — Answer: (D) development of critical thinking.

questions.stem: Children learn more effectively if a concept proceeds from:
questions.explanation: For many children, especially at an early age and during the foundational stages of learning, starting with concrete examples and experiences before moving to abstract concepts is often an effective approach. This method provides a tangible foundation upon which they can build more abstract or theoretical understanding. Concrete experiences make abstract ideas more relatable and comprehensible, helping children grasp complex concepts more effectively.
questions.supporting_excerpt: Children learn more effectively if a concept proceeds from: — Answer: (B) Concrete to Abstract.

options.text: Paritosh known good Bangla; whereas Suchita speakes Hindi.
Saroj got the chance to go to school while Nirmala did dot get the chance to go to school.

Allen belongs to a poor family, while Simon's family is very rich. Language I [English] below and answer the questions that follow by selecting the correct/most appropriate options. Learning a language under any circumstances requires hard work and concentration. However, the circumstances can make a difference in both quality and quantity. Most foreign language students learn in a classroom, from a text-book. In a classroom, language learning can be controlled so that all the necessary structures are taught. Highly motivated students can thus learn the language efficiently and quickly. Learning on the streets and in the markets from experience and need can be effective although the student learns only what he happens to need, in a haphazard way. Some language students find this real-life situation more meaningful because the students success in fulfilling their needs depends on their language ability. However, shop-keepers are more likely to be tolerant of incorrect grammar than classroom teachers, so mispronunciations and errors will not matter much. Nevertheless, the rewards are different for the type of language learning situations. They are immediate (goods, bought in a store) in the real-life but delayed until a quiz or oral recital for the classroom learner. The kind of language learnt in each, setting differs too. In the classroom, the student is more likely to learn the grammatical language of educated people. The language learnt out of necessity often lacks the fine details of the classroom variety and might include informal expressions such as slang. The people learning on the street must be easily understood. Therefore, they might actually sound more like native speakers - although not necessarily educated people. So a combination of classroom

options.text: Imagery Passage 4 The modern youth are more intelligent and hardworking than the previous generations. They have more facilities for education and they do utilise them. But they lack proper direction. In the absence of proper guidance, young boys and girls go on increasing their academic qualifications. Some of them secure high percentage of marks whereas most of them get average or below average marks. Since the number of aspirants for a job is much higher than the number of vacancies, most of the young boys and girls do not get any employment. This causes the problem of the educated unemployment and depression among the youth. The problem of the educated unemployed can be solved partly through proper guidance and counseling and partly through grooming. Young students often disregard the advice of their parents and go on imitating their peers. This sets in the chain of the blind leading the blind. Uneducated or semi-educated parents think of academic qualification as achievement. Young students must seek the advice of the school counselors and select a course of studies that suits their aptitude. Instead of pursuit of academic excellence they must go in for proficiency in technical field of information technology, computers, biotechnology biochemistry and consumer services. In this way their youthful energy will get directed in the proper channel and they may get fruitful employment or become competent enough to launch their own project and give employment to others.

questions.stem: ''I will kill you if you keep on staring without answering me". The voice of the above sentence has been correctly changed in which sentence.

options.text: You had been killed by me if you keep on staring without answering me
You will be killed by me if you keep on staring without answering me
You are being killed by me if you keep on staring without answering me

You were killed by me if you keep on staring without answering me Passage 6 If you have been missing the once-familiar chirping of sparrows around your house, here's your chance to contribute to finding out why this common bird seems to have disappeared from cities across India. A two months long online survey called citizen sparrow was launched inviting responses from people on questions such as when they last sighted the bird and details about the area they live in. ''It is an elementary step to gather information. We are encouraging people to report their experience, be it a drastic drop in sparrow count or a sudden spurt. These inputs will give us valuable leads to compile pan-India data,'' said Suhel Quader, evolutionary ecologist at the National Centre for Biological Sciences. The disappearance of the house sparrow, so widespread till recently that the Chinese Communist Party declared it a pest in 1958 and asked people to exterminate it, remains a great modern mystery world wide. In the UK, sparrows are estimated to have declined from over 12 million to 6 million, since the mid 70s. ''The survey would give us the first baseline data about distribution of sparrows in the country. This would form the basis for further research,'' said Karthik K, project coordinator. The objective of involving ordinary citizens rather than experts comes with a purpose. ''Almost everyone know about sparrows. It is an attempt to reach out to people, asking them to share their stories and their understanding of these birds,'' said Quader. Participants in the survey would be asked to mark locations on a map and give information about their sparrow sightings, including sightings from last year and even earlier. Such information will enable a comparison of population of sparrows in different places and this is expected to point to particular threats or problems. options.text: diminutive CHAPTER 1 : UNSEEN PASSAGE 143 Passage 24 Renowned educationalist Sir Tim Brighouse, observed that an outstanding school has four factors that are visible. ''Teachers talk about teaching, teachers observe each other's practice, teachers plan, organise and evaluate their work together rather than separately and that teachers teach each other.'' He continues ''One of the reasons I like that is that you can immediately see ways in which you could make it more likely that teachers talk about teaching.'' Sir Tim then encouraged schools to focus on activities that were low effort but high impact, describing them as ''butterflies''. Some examples he gave included rotating staff meetings around different classrooms with the host, at the start, describing the room layout and displays or discussing other teaching techniques and approaches. With modern technology teachers could observe their own lessons and then when viewing them back, decide whether they want to share them with a mentor. The role of mentoring was vital and suggested that more schools could send teachers out in small groups to learn from colleagues in other schools. He said ''If this were widespread practice, if people were to attend to their butterflies, the outcome in terms of teacher morale and teacher satisfaction would be positive. We all agree that professional development is the vital ingredient.'' [CTET July 2013]

options.text: sober DIRECTIONS (Poem Nos. 21-30) Read each of the following poem carefully and answer the questions that follow. Poem 21 Common Cold Go hang yourself, you old M.D.! You shall not sneer at me. Pick up your hat and stethoscope Go wash your mouth with laundry soap I contemplate a joy exquisite I'm not paying you for your visit. I did not call you to be told My malady is a common cold. By pounding brow and swollen lip By fever's hot and scaly grip By those two red redundant eyes That weep like woeful April skies By racking snuffle, snort, and sniff By handkerchief after handkerchief This cold you wave away as naught Is the damnedest cold man ever caught! Bacilli swarm within my portals Such as were ne'er conceived by mortals But bred by scientists wise and hoary In some Olympic laboratory Bacteria as large as mice With feet of fire and heads of ice Who never interrupt for slumber Their stamping elephantine rumba. [CTET June 2011]
